summary: Hannover is steering parking by restricting kerbside space, charging for resident permits and pushing cars towards garages. The council adopted the inner-city concept on 29 September 2022 and the Masterplan Mobilität 2035 on 18 December 2025 (21 votes against, 2 abstentions), which lists establishing city parking management as one of ten action areas, and the Umweltzone was lifted on 22 February 2024. In September 2023 the city presented a plan to make the core of the inner city almost car-free by 2030, with kerbside parking largely disappearing and cars led to garages; I did not find whether the council later adopted it. A city FAQ from October 2023 counted about 9,630 spaces in public inner-city garages against 3,843 on the street. The resident permit rose from 30.70 to 96 euros a year with a fee ordinance adopted on 18 December 2025 and, according to the city, effective from 1 February 2026; resident zones A to D, GA to GC (June 2023), F to H (March 2025) and J (November 2025) exist, and further studies are under way. An August 2025 internal draft, reported second-hand via the HAZ, proposed raising the Cityring rate from 2.60 to 4.80 euros an hour; the IHK rejected it, and the ordinance published in January 2026 still lists 2.60 euros an hour in the inner zone and the city's tariff page shows 1.30 euros per half hour. The municipal housing company hanova runs about 5,500 garage spaces and charges 2 to 3 euros for the first hour, while the region's Park & Ride sites are free and, since 2021, partly fitted with occupancy sensors, including the Badenstedt site that opened in March 2024; I found no occupancy statistics for them. The enercity charging-point figures could not be verified.

items.text: A Region Hannover press release (archived on hannover.de; the page itself shows no date, its photo file name is dated 3 May 2021) said its traffic management centre (VMZ) had installed occupancy sensors at five pilot Park & Ride sites, including the Stadtbahn stops Wissenschaftspark Marienwerder (310 spaces) and Nordhafen (180 spaces), that the data were now online, and that more P+R sites with good public-transport service were to be equipped step by step. The region wanted to steer traffic for large events to free P+R spaces and was extending the project to commuters.

On 29 September 2022 (the year shown in the title of the linked decision document) the Hannover council adopted the inner-city concept as an overall concept for a climate-neutral, resilient inner city, a framework to 2035; Mayor Belit Onay called it a broad consensus in the city for a change towards a car-free inner city.
items.source_title: Rat Hannover bringt Innenstadtkonzept auf den Weg

items.text: In late May 2023 the free 10-minute 'Brötchentaste' ticket on Hannover parking machines was abolished and three resident-parking zones in the Südstadt started on 5 June 2023. At that time the highest on-street rate was 2.60 euros per hour, the last fee adjustment dated from 2019 and a resident permit cost 30.70 euros a year.
items.source_title: Parken in Hannover: Diese Pläne hat die Stadt

items.text: The housing and parking company hanova opened its Parkhaus Nordstadt at the KRH Klinikum Nordstadt in May 2023 with 141 spaces, 4 EV charging points, licence-plate entry and cashless payment, built for about 3.4 million euros; tariffs were 2 euros for one hour, 7 euros for 5 hours and 11 euros for 8 to 24 hours. At that date hanova described itself as Hannover's largest garage operator with over 5,500 spaces in 14 garages and about 80 charging points.
items.source_title: Neues Parkhaus am KRH Klinikum Nordstadt

items.text: On 19 September 2023 the city presented a plan (not yet adopted by the council at that time) to make the core of the inner city almost car-free by 2030: on-street parking would largely disappear and cars would be led to the existing garages, which the city described as not nearly fully used so far. I did not find whether the council later adopted this concept.
items.source_title: Stadt Hannover legt Plan für Mobilitätswende in der Innenstadt vor

items.text: Hannover's Umweltzone ended on 22 February 2024, after the council adopted a revised clean-air plan on 25 January 2024; no green sticker is needed on any street in the city since then. The city said nitrogen dioxide annual means had been below the 40 microgram limit at all stations since 2020.

The Park & Ride site at the Stadtbahn stop Hermann-Ehlers-Allee in Badenstedt (line 9) opened on 20 March 2024 with 70 car spaces, sensors that show live occupancy online, and about 800,000 euros of construction cost. It is the 19th Üstra Stadtbahn P+R site and was built to relieve Empelde (80 spaces, mostly full); by April 2024 the regional Infra company said commuters were using Badenstedt only hesitantly, while the 170-space site in Hemmingen was often full.

On 18 August 2025 Radio Hannover reported, citing the HAZ and an internal draft of the city administration, that on-street parking might rise from 2.60 to 4.80 euros an hour inside the Cityring (and from 2.00 to 3.60 euros in nearby districts such as List and Südstadt, from 1.00 to 1.80 euros elsewhere); this was only a draft needing a council majority, aimed at budget gaps and at pushing drivers into garages. I found no source confirming it was adopted.
items.source_title: Stadtverwaltung will Parkgebühren in Hannovers Innenstadt kräftig anheben

items.text: On 18 August 2025 the IHK Hannover rejected the proposed massive rise in on-street parking fees, arguing that businesses in quarters such as Koenigstrasse, List and Suedstadt depend on kerbside parking because few garages are nearby. It called the idea of concentrating parking in garages understandable, but only if garages are easy to reach and attractive, and said this applies to visitors of the pedestrian zone at best with limitations.
items.source_title: IHK lehnt höhere Parkgebühren in Hannover ab

items.text: A headline on electrive.net dated 25 November 2025 says enercity put its 1,000th public charging point in Hannover into operation; the figures in the draft text (888 AC, 112 DC, about 1,300 points by end of 2026, 8.6 electric cars per point) could not be checked.
items.source_title: Enercity nimmt 1.000. öffentlichen Ladepunkt in Hannover in Betrieb

items.text: On 18 December 2025 the Hannover council adopted, against 6 votes, a new fee ordinance (ParkGO) raising the annual resident parking permit from 30.70 to 96 euros, assumed in the council paper to take effect on 1 February 2026. The paper expects up to about 320,000 euros a year extra, based on about 3,900 permits issued by 10 April 2025, and refers to a 2022 budget order to raise parking revenue by 8 million euros a year.

On 18 December 2025 the council adopted the Masterplan Mobilität 2035 (21 votes against, 2 abstentions in the record); one of its ten action areas is to establish city parking management. The plan was introduced in committee on 17 September 2025.

A city page on travel to the Heinz-von-Heiden-Arena (last updated 10 July 2023 according to its footer; read on 21 October 2026) lists recommended Park & Ride sites with Stadtbahn links, including Wissenschaftspark Marienwerder with 300 spaces and Nordhafen with 180 spaces, and says the P+R car parks can be used free of charge and are open around the clock. The 2021 regional press release gives 310 spaces for Marienwerder.
items.source_title: Anreise mit dem Auto: Park & Ride Parkplätze

items.text: The city's FAQ on the inner-city mobility concept (last updated 10 October 2023, before the council had decided on the concept) says there are currently about 9,630 spaces in public garages in the inner city, about 3,843 in public street space and, roughly estimated, about 5,800 on private land. It says garages are busiest on the Advent weekends and generally have capacity to make up for kerb spaces that would be removed.

On the city's parking-machine page, read on 21 October 2026 (its footer says last updated 11 March 2024, yet it links the ParkGO ordinance of 18 December 2025), the inner-city Tarifzone 1 charges 1.30 euros minimum and per half hour (payment required Monday to Saturday 9 a.m. to 8 p.m., 2.5 hours maximum), zone 2 charges 1 euro and zone 3 0.50 euros per half hour; vehicles with an E-plate park free until 31 December 2026 with a parking disc.

A city page on resident parking (last updated 19 February 2026, read on 21 October 2026) says a resident permit costs 96 euros for a year (48 euros for half a year), under a change to the fee ordinance that the city says took effect on 1 February 2026. It lists zones A to D in Mitte (since the 1990s), F, G and H (since March 2025), J (since November 2025) and GA to GC in Suedstadt/Bult (since June 2023), and says studies are under way on whether resident zones can be set up in Nordstadt, Vahrenwald, List, Zoo, Bult and Suedstadt, with concepts also being prepared for quarters such as the Oststadt.

On the page read on 21 October 2026 hanova lists 8 inner-city garages, 4 district garages and 3 car parks with about 5,500 spaces, mostly cashless-only. A first hour costs 2.50 euros in Mehlstraße, Altstadt/Schmiedestraße, Osterstraße, Andreaestraße and Karolinenstraße (19 euros for 9 to 24 hours), 3 euros at Oper/Kröpcke and Windmühlenstraße (25 euros a day) and 2 euros an hour at Hbf/Raschplatz (18 euros a day).

On the regional traffic management centre's fairgrounds page (undated, read on 21 October 2026) it says there are 28,000 parking spaces for cars and coaches near the Messe and that the parking guidance system on the Messering leads arriving traffic to the lots intended for each event or fair.

gaps: Browser pane tab could not be opened, so pages were downloaded as raw HTML over HTTP and converted to text; no JavaScript-rendered content (VMZ live P+R occupancy, Parkleitsystem city page, Hanova booking pages) could be read

Whether the 4.80 euros per hour draft (August 2025) was adopted: the unsigned ordinance annex to Drucksache 2352/2025 (https://e-government.hannover-stadt.de/lhhsimwebdd.nsf/315B0458770D7711C1258D3F0033927B/$FILE/2352-2025_Anlage1.pdf) still lists zone I at 2.60 euros per hour and 96 euros for permits, but no source on a rate decision was found; the HAZ original was not opened
Council decision on the 2023 Mobilitätskonzept Innenstadt (almost car-free centre by 2030) and on the Georgstraße rebuild: only the 2023 plan and the August 2025 progress report were found
No utilisation or occupancy figures for Wissenschaftspark Marienwerder, Hermann-Ehlers-Allee or Nordhafen; capacity for Marienwerder differs between sources (310 in 2021, 300 on the city arena page)

Third-party garage operators (Contipark, APCOA, Q-Park, Ernst-August-Galerie, Kaufhof, Galerie Luise) and the Parkleitsystem city installation date and tariff page (http://www.vmz-niedersachsen.de/hannover/parkleitsystem-city/ returned 404) were not opened
